name: Alkoclar height treatment

card.summary: A patented formula associated with Turkish inventor Erdal Can Alkoclar that is claimed to add height in growing people, discussed in height-increase forums as an alternative to hormone-based approaches.
card.aka: alkoclar; Erdal Can Alkoclar; Alkoclar formula
card.note: Results have not been published in peer-reviewed form; forum members report a high price and describe reported side effects from earlier versions.

quick.overview:
Alkoclar is the name used on height forums for a patented formulation and programme linked to Erdal Can Alkoclar, a Turkish inventor. It is described as a growth-supporting formula for children and young adults, and forum posters repeat claims that it can add several centimetres of height within a year.

The topic is discussed mainly on looksmax.org. Posts cite a patent describing a somatotropic composition and quote statements attributed to Alkoclar about results and side effects, but no peer-reviewed trial results are cited in those threads.
quick.how: According to forum posters, the formula is obtained directly from Alkoclar as a year-long supply, taken alongside a routine, with growth said to depend on age and open growth plates. These accounts are second-hand and the product details are not independently documented here.
quick.risks: One forum poster quotes a statement attributed to the inventor that earlier chronic-use versions caused side effects, including carpal-tunnel-like symptoms and prostate effects in some participants. Forum members also raise concerns about the cost, long timeline and refund terms. No regulator approval is cited.

lead: The Alkoclar height treatment refers, in looksmaxxing and height-increase forums, to a formulation and programme associated with Erdal Can Alkoclar, a Turkish scientist and entrepreneur. Forum posts describe him as holder of many patents, including one for a somatotropic composition intended for dwarfism and late-growth conditions.[1][3]

People interested in height discuss it as a possible way for adolescents and young adults to gain several centimetres, with one thread poster repeating a story of a young man growing almost 8 cm in under a year.[3] Another thread describes the claimed routine as adding 5 to 8 cm.[2]

The claims come from forum discussion and statements attributed to the inventor. Posts say he announced closing a study without publishing all the data, and describe side effects in earlier versions of the formula.[1] No clinical studies are cited in the threads.

chain: Claimed to act on growth in people with open growth plates
Claimed gain of several centimetres in a year
angle.text: Proponents say the formula can increase height in younger people, with figures like 5 to 8 cm mentioned in forums. These figures are reported by posters and not backed by published trial data in the cited threads.

infobox: About 7,000 euros for a year's supply (forum reports)

paras: A forum poster describes Alkoclar as a Turkish scientist and millionaire who claimed some years ago to have discovered a compound that makes people grow, originally framed as a medicine for achondroplasia.[1] A quoted statement attributed to him says his former R&D team patented more than 154 methylprotodioscin derivatives with uses ranging from neurogenesis and myogenesis to height increase, while noting inconsistent results from the oral formulation.[1]
One thread describes a patent as a somatotropic composition that helps dwarfism and late growth syndromes and increases expression of a growth-related mRNA.[3]

Forum users report that the formula is offered as a year's supply at about 7,000 euros with a money-back guarantee, and that free trials have been promised for years but not delivered; these are individual accounts.[2][3] One poster, aged 18, wrote that he planned to try it and described earlier use of other height approaches such as hormone products.[3]
Other members questioned the reliability of the claims, arguing that a large pharmaceutical company would have bought a formula that worked.[3]

In one thread a poster states that 4 of 7 participants in an earlier study experienced severe carpal-tunnel-like symptoms with loss of limb function and that participants also had prostate inflammation and raised PSA levels.[1] These statements are second-hand forum quotations.

lore.intro: The formula is discussed on looksmax.org as a possible alternative to growth-hormone-based height approaches, with debate over its legitimacy and price.[2][3]

claims.claim: The formula can add 5 to 8 cm of height in a year
claims.believers: Posters repeat that it made a young man grow almost 8 cm in under a year and that younger users with open growth plates respond best.[3]
claims.experts: No published trial or peer-reviewed report in the cited threads supports the figure.

claims.claim: The inventor is a credentialed scientist with patents, so the formula is credible
claims.believers: A poster cites his recognition as a scientist and inventor with several patents and a 100% refund promise as reasons to take it seriously.[3]
claims.experts: Patent filings describe a composition but are not clinical evidence of height gain; other members in the same thread raised doubts.[3]

claims.claim: Earlier versions caused serious side effects
claims.believers: A quoted statement attributed to the inventor says side effects from chronic use could not be sufficiently reduced, and a poster lists carpal-tunnel-like symptoms and prostate changes.[1]
claims.experts: No independent safety data are cited.
